question: The function $f$ is defined by $$f(x)=\begin{cases}\frac{x^2-9}{x-3}, & x\neq 3\\k, & x=3\end{cases}$$ Determine the value of $k$ so that $f$ is continuous at $x=3$.
explanation:
Simplifying the function near $x=3$
For $x\neq 3$, $$f(x)=\frac{(x-3)(x+3)}{x-3}=x+3$$
Limit at $x=3$
$$\lim_{x\to 3}f(x)=\lim_{x\to 3}(x+3)=6$$
Continuity condition
For continuity at $x=3$, $$\lim_{x\to 3}f(x)=f(3)$$
Since $f(3)=k$, $$k=6$$
Therefore, the required value is $k=6$.
